data.content_ref: inline:The target's central defense rests on verisimilitude ('truth-likeness') as a load-bearing concept linking corroboration to proximity to truth. But the Tichý/Miller result (1974) is not a hypothetical countercondition — it is an established mathematical proof that Popper's own definition of verisimilitude cannot order false theories by truth-likeness. Since Popper holds that all tested scientific theories are strictly false (conjectures that will eventually be superseded), there are NO true theories to compare, and verisimilitude comparisons among false theories are exactly what the definition fails to deliver. The target relegates this to a conditional countercondition ('If the Tichý/Miller proof holds...'), but the proof does hold, which means the claim that 'corroboration tracks truth-likeness' is not merely at risk — it is already defeated. The defense can survive on informational content alone, but the claim explicitly couples the two ('based on verisimilitude and informational content'), and verisimilitude contributes nothing once the formal comparison is impossible. Thus the target overstates the defensibility of the Popperian position by presenting an already-refuted mathematical obstacle as a live but unresolved contingency.
